text:
perf-bot: :warning: Nightly perf alert: tail latency for small-seq (<=64) gen workload increased by ~28% vs baseline, throughput down ~12%. Affected service: runtime-execpath. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.ai/nightly/perf/execpath

aria: saw the alert, digging in. any obvious recent merges to execpath?

thomas: 4307 landed yesterday into main — it changed the kernel cost model (cost-estimator v2) and also flips dynamic-fallback to enabled by default. we should check that. PR: https://git.redwood.ai/4307

samir: running a quick bisect on the nightly images now. locally i can reproduce a ~20% tail bump when using kernel cost-estimator v2 + tight batch windows.

jessica: CI nightly perf job also flagged it earlier: `ci/nightly/execpath-bench` failed on the small-seq suite. failure log: `p50 12ms -> 14.8ms, p95 28ms -> 36.5ms`. attaching snippet.

lin: pinging the runtime telemetry: allocation churn looks normal, but KV cache hit rate dropped ~6% at the same time window. possible interaction between kernel selection and KV cache prefetching?

samir: profiler (flamegraph) for an affected request: hot path shows increased time in `kernel_selector::evaluate_candidates` and `execpath::fallback_dispatch`. looks like when cost model picks the new kernel, we hit a path that triggers a synchronous KV cache refill more often. snippet:
```
# perf script summary (collapsed)
kernel_selector::evaluate_candidates  38%
execpath::fallback_dispatch         22%
kv_cache::sync_prefetch             15%
other                               25%
```

aria: interesting — so cost-estimator picks a kernel that forces a different memory layout and that interacts poorly with our KV prefetching heuristic. any quick mitigations?

thomas: two options: (A) revert 4307 on main and release branches until we have a patch, or (B) tweak batch-window-scheduler to avoid the pathological branch for small sequences (fast fix).

jessica: release-bot showed a rolling canary using main that started at 02:10 UTC — that correlates with the first regression spike. if we revert main, can we cut a hotfix to stable?

lin: i ran a targeted microbenchmark: switching cost-estimator back to v1 restores baseline numbers. so reverting is likely to fix it.

samir: bisect result: commit 7c3d9bf (PR 4307 merge commit) is the first bad commit. git bisect log attached.
```
# git bisect log
bisect start
bad 7c3d9bf
good 6a2f4ab
# first bad commit 7c3d9bf
```

aria: ok let's revert on main and branch a hotfix for stable. thomas, can you open the revert PR and tag release? also add a test that runs small-seq microbench in CI.

thomas: opening revert PR now. Title: "revert: kernel cost-estimator v2 default enable (revert 7c3d9bf)". tagging @release. will include perf numbers pre/post in PR body.

release-bot: Note: cutting hotfix branch `hotfix/execpath-revert-4307` from `release/2026-03-14` as requested. CI triggered: https://ci.redwood.ai/job/hotfix-execpath

jessica: after revert canary patched on staging, we should monitor KV hit-rate and small-seq tail. also add a dashboard annotation for the revert timestamp.

lin: follow-ups: (1) root cause: cost-estimator scoring function returned preference for kernel that causes extra synchronous KV prefetch; need to update estimator to include `kv_prefetch_penalty` in score. (2) add `nightly/microbench-small-seq` to CI (short, ~2min) as a guard. (3) add telemetry flag to sample kernel selection decisions per-request.

aria: thanks all. Samir — can you post the flamegraph artifacts to the thread and mark heatmap ranges? will be helpful for the estimator patch.

samir: uploaded artifacts to: https://artifacts.redwood.ai/flame/1871234567-execpath. leaving notes in the PR.

thomas: PR created: https://git.redwood.ai/revert-4307. CI baseline numbers attached. planning to merge after one +1 and confirmation from perf.

aria: great. moving this to high priority. if revert fixes nightly, we'll ship hotfix and then schedule a proper follow-up to reintroduce estimator v2 behind an opt-in and with the extra tests. :white_check_mark:

perf-bot: update: canary on staging shows tail latency back within 3% of baseline after revert. will keep monitoring next 24h.
